claims.claim: 1. BlockFtsEntry and PageFtsEntry are full-text tables: FTS4, standalone (no contentEntity), simple tokenizer, columns pageId/plainText and pageId/blockId/plainText

evidence.quote: "createSql": "CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `${TABLE_NAME}` USING FTS4(`pageId` INTEGER NOT NULL, `plainText` TEXT NOT NULL)",
"createSql": "CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `${TABLE_NAME}` USING FTS4(`pageId` INTEGER NOT NULL, `blockId` INTEGER NOT NULL, `plainText` TEXT NOT NULL)",

claims.claim: 2. Index maintained by application code, not triggers (neither Room-generated nor hand-written)
3. Searchable via FTS: pages (title + concatenated block text) and blocks only. No entries, tasks, habits, labels, or journal/check-ins in any FTS table

evidence.quote: Page::class, Label::class, PageLabel::class, Block::class, PageFtsEntry::class, BlockFtsEntry::class,

claims.claim: 4. Query: MATCH with a * prefix on each alphanumeric token, ANDed. Input is sanitised by keeping only letter/digit runs. There is no ORDER BY and no bm25/matchinfo ranking. snippet() gives the highlight, and ranking happens in Kotlin (title prefix first, then block hits in index order, at most 3 per page)

evidence.quote: "WHERE block_fts MATCH :query AND pages.deletedAt IS NULL LIMIT 60"

claims.claim: 5. Search over non-indexed tables uses LIKE: block-reference picker and unlinked-mentions use a substring scan over blocks.content, and label search uses a substring scan over tags.name

evidence.quote: "AND blocks.content LIKE '%' || :query || '%' ORDER BY blocks.updatedAt DESC LIMIT 30"
@Query("SELECT * FROM tags WHERE name LIKE '%' || :query || '%' ORDER BY name")

claims.claim: 6. Index is rebuilt after sync merge and Notion import, and rebuilt at startup by healIndex. The FTS tables are not part of the sync payload, since nothing in sync/ references them except the per-page rebuild

missed.fact: The switcher's body search reads only block_fts (QuickSwitcher.kt:144). page_fts is still written on every rebuild, but the switcher does not use its MATCH query. PagesViewModel and PagesScreen take a PageFtsDao.
page_fts stores the page title as the first token run of plainText (title + block contents joined by a space). One column carries both meanings, and block_fts holds block content only, with no title.
The FTS tables carry no deletedAt of their own. Trashed pages are hidden only by the JOIN pages ... pages.deletedAt IS NULL in each search query. A page's rows are not removed on soft delete.

Identity columns: pageId is a plain indexed column in both tables (not UNIQUE). blockId in block_fts is the local Room blocks.id, not the cross-device uid, so the index cannot be merged between devices and has to be rebuilt locally. Sync does that per merged page.

block_fts was added in schema v25 with a virtual-table-only migration. The first-launch healIndex fills it. MIGRATION_15_16 also empties page_fts so the titles get indexed, and a later healIndex run re-indexes everything. healIndex only re-indexes pages with no row in an index, so an existing stale row is never repaired.
Both search() queries have hard LIMITs (50 for pages, 60 for blocks) applied before the Kotlin ranking and per-page cap of 3. There is no ORDER BY, so which rows survive the LIMIT is unspecified.

The block-reference picker and unlinked-mentions search (BlockDao.searchContent) excludes templates and the types BLOCK_REFERENCE, DIVIDER, IMAGE, CANVAS and PAGE_MENTION. This differs from the FTS indexes, which index every block with non-blank content.

absence_probes.pattern: tokenize in FTS context / tokenizer args (only the schema JSON default 'simple'; kt hits are unrelated formula/highlight lexers)
@Fts4/@Fts5 entities for entries, tasks, habits, labels, journal/check-ins (only PageFtsEntry and BlockFtsEntry exist in TendrilDatabase entities)
